{"notes": "Visit 2, left at 2:45. Table: about 130 dominoes, all dark (connected to the start). Both lines leave the nose and run right with smooth curves. The top line runs through the S-bend up to a tail curl near (28,6). The bottom line runs to about (26,15). The tail is not closed: there is a large gap between the two line ends, roughly from (28,6) down to (26,15). I don't know who placed which domino, so I credit no one for placement.

Maya: Moved from sketching to coaching. She named the nose-connection point ('the whole run still falls from the nose'), gave Priya a specific caution about the lower pinch, and offered Leo help while respecting his ownership. Her check-in is good, with clear communication and low ego. Watch: she has offered to help but I haven't seen her build. Leo asked her to close the gap, so see whether she does it and checks the joints.

Tom: Silent this visit. Leo thanked him for something I didn't hear, so he may have helped Leo. Ask Leo what it was. Otherwise no direct evidence. His earlier point about the connection to the start looks right, since the structure is intact.

Priya: Still silent, but the bottom line looks well advanced and connected. Maya's remark suggests she's been building steadily. Ask her privately how she's finding it, and whether she knows Leo wants her line to meet the tail.

Leo: Spoke up for the first time. He kept ownership of the tail, explained why (one stroke, avoiding collisions), and named exactly where he needs help: the gap where Priya's line stops short of the tail's lower end. That is clear, and he handled Maya's offer well. Risk: the tail is the long piece and the gap is still open at 2:45.

Team risk: closing the tail joint between Priya's line and Leo's tail. Check on visit 3 that it is closed and connected."}
